$comment: VAPP-33: steer over eNet's chat channel (`exp/enet/chat/1`, acked, ONE ordered stream per peer) between a viewer install and the install RUNNING the session. The steer frames themselves are unchanged (apps/steer-relay/src/protocol.ts + STEER-WIRE-EXP-850.md); only the carrier moves. ENVELOPE: one chat message = UTF-8 JSON `{t:"exp-steer", v:1, sessionId, frames:[...]}`, frames = wire frame OBJECTS (never strings), applied in array order, envelopes in chat order. `parse` rules (every receiver): t must be `exp-steer`, v must be 1, sessionId a non-empty string, frames a NON-EMPTY array of objects each with a string `t` (the wire frames' own tag, exactly the relay's `{t:"input",data}` etc.); anything else is not a steer envelope (ignored, acked). A frame whose `t` the receiver does not know is skipped, the rest of the envelope still applies. VIEWER → DEVICE frames: `join {channel:"activity"}`, `leave`, and the relay client frames `input`, `answer`, `interrupt`, `unqueue`, `set_config`, `set_mode`, `kill`, `history_page {requestId, beforeSeq, limit}` (its session is the envelope's), `search` (#EDE-96, `search.$comment`). Frames go out exactly as on the relay socket (e.g. `{t:"join",channel:"activity"}`, `{t:"answer",questionId,keys,text?}`). DEVICE → VIEWER: on `join` = `activity_reset`, the journal replay (`activity {event, seq}` in `replay_seq` order: the log, then the latest-wins slots; only its REPLAY TAIL, below), then `activity_synced {firstSeq, lastSeq, truncated?}` (the end-of-replay marker, exactly the relay's: firstSeq/lastSeq = the seqs of the first and last LOG entry (the latest-wins slots do not count), both 0 when the log is empty; `truncated: true` when the journal evicted, the REPLAY TAIL left older events out, or firstSeq > 0, absent otherwise); REPLAY TAIL (large chats: a 16 MiB journal of ~17k events took seconds to open on every viewer): a join replays only the newest `steerFeed.replayTail` LOG events, contiguous, plus every latest-wins slot; the cut moves back (by at most another `replayTail`) so the kept log holds the `tool` row of every kept `tool_update` and every question no `question_resolved` retired; older events reach the viewer only through `history_page` (reference `steer::history::replay_tail`). A RESUMED run on the device that already holds the session's journal file (under its cap) seeds its replay from that file and never records the agent's history replay again (the events it streams back before the host seeds the `turn` slot): appending it stacked one copy of the conversation per resume (21 in a real 16 MiB file). LEGACY REPLAYS: a file written before that still holds the copies (up to 137 of one call); every read of the file (`steer::history::read_journal_seq`: a join's replay, `history_page`, the desktop's own read) drops only what it can PROVE is a replayed copy and keeps everything else: a `tool` whose call id an earlier line holds; a `narration`/`thought` of a message already over (by `messageId`, per agent lane) whose text that message already showed; a `tool_update` identical (minus `at`) to the latest of its id; any other row identical (minus `at`) to an earlier one only when the next decisive line in its `turn`-free stretch is such a copy (a live prompt is answered by a `turn` edge or new ids, so a prompt sent twice stays twice). Kept events keep their line's seq (sparse, never renumbered); the file is never rewritten. Every viewer pages them in when the reader scrolls within one viewport of the transcript's top (the same action as its `Load earlier` button, no new UI); afterwards every recorded event live as `activity {event, seq}`; `history_chunk {requestId, events, seqs, done}` to the asker only; `keepalive` every `keepaliveMs` to every joined viewer; `bye {outcome}` when the run ends (the viewer is dropped); `error {code}` with `no_such_session` (this install neither runs the session live nor holds its stored journal: the viewer tries its next endpoint) or `unauthorized` (the access rule). STORED REPLAY (VAPP-43, replaces the relay's `history_request` + lingering rooms): a `join` for a session this install does not run live but whose journal file it holds (EXP-773 `{data_dir}/journal/<sessionId>.jsonl`) is answered from the file under the same access rule, the audience (team, starter, shared) read off the device's synced `sessions` row (no row = `no_such_session`): `activity_reset`, the file's replay (`read_journal_seq`, its REPLAY TAIL), `activity_synced` (`truncated` only when the tail left older events out), then, for an ENDED row, `bye {outcome:"history"}` (the viewer is dropped); for a row still alive (idle: its run went away between turns) the viewer stays joined: `keepalive`s, `history_page` answered from the file, and once the run's publisher comes back on this install every such viewer is handed to it as a fresh join (`activity_reset` + replay). A re-sent `join` restarts the feed (activity_reset + replay), exactly like a relay reconnect. STORED TAIL (#PERF-9, the phones' cold open: the join + replay took 250–525 ms before the first row): a viewer install keeps, per session it opened, the newest `storedTail` events its feed applied (`activity` events with their seqs, the replay's and the live ones) plus only the LATEST of each latest-wins slot kind (`turn`, `usage`, `queue`, `rate_limit`, `diff`…: a working agent's `turn` every few seconds would push every row out), written off the main thread and debounced; for a root with a tree key (`sessions.seal_public_key`) the tail is stored SEALED as one body envelope (`exp-sealed:v1:<epoch>:…`, sealed-content.json) over its JSON with the tree's current key, never in clear (nothing opened is written back in clear); a keyless tree's tail is stored as is. Opening the session paints that tail at once as the transcript (the same rows, no new UI, `Load earlier` after it as usual) while discovery and the `join` run; the join's `activity_reset` + replay then REPLACES it without a placeholder frame (the reader's anchor holds, EXP-656). A tail that does not open (no key here yet, malformed) is not shown; signing out of the account deletes its tails. PRUNING (LRU, per account): opening a session stamps its tail's last use; a tail not opened within `storedTailMaxAgeDays` is deleted, and beyond the `storedTailMaxSessions` most recently opened only the newest stay (whichever rule keeps fewer), checked off the main thread whenever a tail is written. BATCHING (the device): a viewer's feed drains its queue into one envelope while the serialized envelope stays ≤ `batchMaxBytes`; a frame that alone passes it goes in an envelope of its own; an envelope over `chatMaxBytes` (enet-core MAX_CHAT_MESSAGE) is never sent (the frame is dropped and logged). A failed or timed-out (`sendTimeoutMs`) send drops the viewer. DISCOVERY: the viewer calls tRPC `installs.forSession {sessionId}` → `[{endpointId, kind}]` = the non-revoked `desktop`/`daemon` installs whose `device_id` = the session's `device_id`, newest `last_seen_at` first, only for a caller who can see the session (the visibility rule: starter, or `shared` + team member). It sends `join` to the first; on `error no_such_session` the next; no endpoint, no node, every endpoint refused, or no `activity_synced` within `joinTimeoutMs` of that endpoint's join (#EXP-1679) = NO FEED on eNet: the viewer falls back to the SEALED RELAY TUNNEL (`fallback` below, #EXP-1525) and shows NO FEED only when that carrier fails too. The viewer shows its EXISTING states with their existing copy: a row still alive = `starting` ("The live stream isn't up yet. The desktop may still be connecting.") and redials on its backoff; an ended row = `ended` with the device-offline copy ("{device} is offline. The transcript lives on that machine."). A viewer that sees no frame for `staleMs` re-sends `join`. OFFLINE REDIAL (VAPP-169): the device-offline `ended` is NOT terminal: the viewer keeps the session open and redials (discovery + `join`, the same path) when the session's device flips ONLINE in presence (the synced devices row), on a wakeup (app foreground, network back) and every `staleMs` while that copy shows (presence lags, or is off). The redial holds the phase (no `connecting` flash); NO FEED again = the same copy, a feed = the transcript (a stored replay ending in `bye history` = the plain `ended`, a run that came back = `live`). An `ended` reached by `bye` (the transcript is on screen) never redials; a `starting` row cuts its backoff short on a presence flip online or a wakeup and otherwise redials on its backoff, never on the stale timer. A presence flip OFFLINE never dials. SUBSCRIPTIONS (EXP-1487, the viewer install): several viewers of one session on one install (the desktop agent screen's transcript and its root composer) share the device's ONE feed for that endpoint: every subscriber gets every frame of the session from that device (fan-out, never a replace), a `join` from any of them restarts the shared feed for all (`activity_reset` + replay, each applies it), and only the LAST subscriber of the session to that device sends `leave`. A second viewer never ends the first's feed. LOST BANNER (EXP-1487): a feed that was live and drops (a failed send, a closed subscription, the stale timer, NO FEED or an error on the redial) redials SILENTLY on its backoff: the phase holds (the transcript stays, no "Connection lost", no `connecting` flash); a successful join resets the count. The "Connection lost" banner (with Reconnect) shows only once the feed has been down at least `lostBanner.graceMs` since the drop AND at least `lostBanner.failedRedials` redials since the drop failed; until then the drop is invisible. An ended row's device-offline copy and `starting` keep their own rules above. `lostBanner` cases: {downMs (since the drop), failedRedials} → show. NO FEED, EMPTY TRANSCRIPT (EXP-1487): what a viewer with nothing to show says while NO FEED holds, keyed on the synced row: an ENDED row = the device-offline copy above; a BUSY row (a turn is running) = `starting` (spinner + "The agent is starting. Waiting for the live stream…"); a row that is NOT busy and not ended (idle, waiting for its next message, or on an open question: `needsInput`) is never `starting`: it shows the `idle` empty state (no spinner) with `noFeedIdle.title` / `noFeedIdle.text` (web's existing "No live transcript" state) while it keeps redialing on its backoff; a feed replaces it with the transcript. SENT INPUTS (Android 0.14.134: "started a new session, nothing happens"): while a session view shows ANY no-feed placeholder (the feed is EMPTY) of a row that is not ended, the session's own card-less person inputs the device already CONSUMED (`authorKind` user, `card` null, `consumedAt` set; a not-consumed one, and the composer's outbox, follow them as the own tail of message-delivery.json, #FEED-237: ONE own-bubble mechanism, each bubble with its time and delivery mark, a consumed input reading `read`) draw as the viewer's own message bubbles above the placeholder's copy, oldest first (`createdAt`, then `id`), at most the newest `noFeedInputsMax` (reference `steerNoFeedInputs`, `noFeedInputCases`): the brief a claim consumes at once is the first, so a session started from a phone shows what was sent before its device publishes; a feed replaces them (its replay holds them as `user_message`). A QUEUED row (not yet claimed) with NO FEED reads "Starting on {device}" (feedback-states.json), never the idle state. ROW WAKE (same report): a `starting` row's backoff is also cut short by its SYNCED ROW saying its device has it now: `status` leaving `queued` (the claim) or turning `running`, `busy` turning true (a turn started) or `deviceId` changing (a move), and the backoff restarts at n = 0 (a change that lands while a dial is out redials as soon as that dial says NO FEED); any other row change waits the backoff out (reference `steerRowWakes(from, to)`, `rowWakeCases`). #EXP-1703 (owner 2026-11-05) A DEVICE THAT IS AWAY: a row NOT ended whose host device is OFFLINE in presence (the synced devices row; unknown = online) shows `away` instead of `starting`/`idle`: the page EmptyState titled `noFeedAway.title` with {device} = the device name (unknown = `noFeedAway.device`), text `noFeedAway.text`, no spinner; what the viewer already holds (its local-first cache of the feed) shows as the transcript instead, exactly like any feed. The viewer treats it as the device-offline phase: OFFLINE REDIAL below (presence online, wakeup, staleMs), never the starting backoff, so an away device is not dialled every few seconds. `noFeed` cases: {ended, busy, needsInput, deviceOffline (absent = false)} → state (`offline`, `away`, `starting`, `idle`), ended first, then away. `offlineRedial` cases: {phase (`offline` = the device-offline ended, `ended` = ended by `bye`, `starting`), trigger (`presenceOnline`, `presenceOffline`, `staleTimer`, `wakeup`)} → redial. ACCESS (the device, per envelope): the sender endpoint's user comes from the registry list of the SESSION's team (`installs.list {teamId: sessions.team_id}` entries; an endpoint known only from another team the device's user shares with the sender does NOT count); unknown endpoint = refused; the starter (`sessions.user_id`) = allowed; another user = allowed only when the session is `shared` (being in that team's list = a member). `access` cases: {viewerUserId (null = endpoint not in the session team's registry list), starterUserId, shared} → allowed. VIEWER SIDE: device frames arrive as chat messages the DEVICE dials (each side sends on its own outbound stream, so the viewer's allowlist must hold the device's endpoint: the same team registry); the viewer applies only envelopes whose sessionId it joined AND whose sender is the endpoint it joined, every other steer envelope is ignored. `parse` cases: {body (the chat body as a JSON value, or bodyText for a raw string)} → {ok, sessionId?, types? (the frames' `t` tags kept, in order)}. `batch` cases: frame sizes in bytes (each frame's serialized JSON length) with the envelope overhead `overhead` (the serialized envelope with an empty frames array) and one comma per extra frame → the groups as frame indexes; `dropped` = indexes over chatMaxBytes even alone. #FEED-260 (Danny, 2026-11-16: a chat showed the request and `Ran 3 commands` but not the agent's synced answer, its device offline) SYNCED TAIL ×4: the transcript is the device's feed, but every SYNCED message of the session shows whether or not the device is reachable. While the viewer's feed is NOT live (a stored tail painted at open, the cache of a dropped feed, an empty feed), the session's synced messages AFTER that feed draw after its last row as ordinary transcript rows (an agent's = the agent's narration bubble, a person's = their input bubble, each with its `createdAt` time), reference `steerSyncedTail({live, feed, messages, max})`, `syncedTailCases`: a live feed = none (the feed is the authority); a message counts when it is card-less with a non-blank body and is the agent's (`authorKind` agent) or a person's input the device CONSUMED (`authorKind` user, `consumedAt` set; a not-consumed one is the own tail / Dock queue); `system` never; it is AFTER the feed when its `createdAt` is later than the feed's newest known row time (`at`: a narration's first fragment, an input, a settled tool; a non-empty feed with no known time places nothing); a message the feed already holds is dropped (an agent line whose trimmed body equals, or is a prefix of or prefixed by, a main-lane narration's trimmed text; an input whose trimmed body equals a feed input's); oldest first (`createdAt`, then `id`), the newest `syncedTailMax`. An EMPTY feed takes the tail only while its live transcript cannot be loaded (`unreachable`: the OFFLINE LINE's condition below, absent = false; a reachable device's replay is on its way and holds the same lines) and only when it holds an agent line (then the inputs come with it and the transcript replaces the no-feed placeholder); otherwise SENT INPUTS above keeps the placeholder. The feed's join replay then replaces the tail (its rows hold the same lines). OFFLINE LINE: a transcript that is not live and shows rows (feed or tail) ENDS with THE inline marker (the `Context compacted` row's centred muted label) reading `noFeedAway.title` ({device} as above) when the live transcript cannot be loaded: an ended row whose last dial said NO FEED (the device-offline copy), a row not ended whose host device is offline in presence; never while live, never under a placeholder (the placeholder says it), reference `steerOfflineLine({live, rows, ended, noFeed, deviceOffline})`, `offlineLineCases`.

fallback.$comment: SEALED RELAY FALLBACK (P2P stabilisation, 2026-11-01). eNet stays the PRIMARY carrier; the steer relay comes back as a FALLBACK that carries CIPHERTEXT ONLY, used automatically when eNet stalls or drops, never raced against it. CARRIER: the same exp-steer envelopes (every rule above: join, replay, live, keepalive, bye, error, history_page, batching) ride a relay TUNNEL instead of an eNet chat stream; every envelope is SEALED to the session TREE key (fixtures/sealed-content.json): tunnel `data` = `v1:<epoch>:<b64url push_seal(tree_public, utf8(envelope JSON))>` (the sealed-value grammar after the body prefix; opened with openBody(`exp-sealed:` + data)), in both directions; a data that does not open (noKey, refused, malformed, unsupported) or does not parse as an envelope of the tunnel's session is dropped. The relay sees the sessionId, the tunnel id and the ciphertext, nothing else. AVAILABILITY (the viewer): the relay leg exists only when the ROOT has a seal key (`sessions.seal_public_key`) AND this install holds the tree secret of its current epoch AND tRPC `steer.tunnelTicket {sessionId}` returns a ticket (the caller passes the visibility rule and the session's host device is online on the relay with `tunnel: 1`); otherwise it is `relayUnavailable` and the viewer behaves exactly as eNet-only. TICKET: role `tunnel`, claims {sub (the viewer user), team, sessionId, deviceId (the host's steer device id), deviceOwnerId}; the relay admits it only while that device's control socket announced `tunnel: 1`, else answers `{t:"tunnel_error", code}` (`device_offline` | `device_unsupported`) and closes. WIRE: viewer socket <-> relay = `{t:"sealed", data}` both ways (+ `tunnel_error` relay -> viewer). Relay <-> device CONTROL socket: `online {deviceId, tunnel: 1}` (an older device omits it), relay -> device `tunnel_open {tunnelId, sessionId, userId}` then `tunnel_data {tunnelId, data}` per viewer frame, `tunnel_close {tunnelId}` when the viewer socket goes; device -> relay `tunnel_data {tunnelId, data}` (forwarded to that viewer socket as `sealed`) and `tunnel_close {tunnelId}` (the relay closes the viewer socket). `tunnelId` = relay-minted, unique per viewer socket. A data longer than `tunnelMaxDataBytes` is dropped. THE DEVICE treats a tunnel exactly like an eNet viewer endpoint: the access rule with viewerUserId = the tunnel's `userId` (the relay took it from the server-minted ticket), the same live fan-out, stored replay, keepalive and bye; a device without the tree secret answers nothing but `tunnel_close`. THE RULE (every viewer, `carrierCases`, reducer `steerCarrierStep(state, event) -> {state, actions}`): state = {active: `none` | `enet` | `relay`, relay: `closed` | `open`}. `start` dials eNet and arms the stall timer (`stallMs`); `stall` (no eNet frame by then) or `enetNoFeed` (no endpoint, no node, a failed join send, join timeout) while nothing is active opens the relay; `enetRefused` (#EXP-1678: EVERY endpoint ANSWERED the join with `error` (`no_such_session`, `unauthorized`) or `bye`: the device itself said no, and the relay tunnel reaches that same device) opens NO relay leg: nothing active and no relay = NO FEED at once (the connection's `starting` redial takes it from there), a relay already opening answers for itself, a relay already active keeps eNet redialing (`redialEnetLater`); a join that could not be SENT is `send_failed` (an `enetNoFeed`), never `refused`; a drop of the active eNet feed opens (or re-joins) the relay AT ONCE and redials eNet on its backoff; while the relay is active eNet keeps redialing in the background (`redialEnetLater`) and the eNet feed's `activity_reset` takes over (`apply`), the relay closing once that feed delivers `activity_synced`; frames apply only from the active carrier (`apply`) and are dropped otherwise (`drop`); a carrier's `activity_reset` with nothing active makes it active. Steering frames (input, answer, interrupt, ...) go out on the ACTIVE carrier. VISIBLE STATE: carriers are invisible: the phase, the transcript and the copy never name one; the lostBanner rule counts from the moment NEITHER carrier is active and counts failed redials of BOTH; NO FEED (noFeed above) = both failed (eNet no feed and relay unavailable, dropped or not synced within joinTimeoutMs). STARTING REDIAL (#EXP-1678, `startingRetry`): a row still alive with NO FEED (`starting`, or the idle state) redials on an equal-jitter backoff: the n-th consecutive NO FEED (n from 0) waits a random delay in [cap/2, cap) with cap = min(baseMs * 2^n, maxMs) (`startingRetryCases`: retries -> capMs, reference `steerStartingRetryCapMs`); a feed resets n, a wakeup (presence online, app foreground, network back) cuts the wait short; a redial with nothing active and no relay leg is a new `start` (#EXP-1679: eNet dials and the stall timer re-arms), so the relay's next try never waits for a slow eNet attempt to fail. FALLBACK COUNT (#EXP-1678): `connStats.fallbacks` counts a relay leg only once it is AVAILABLE on this install (the root has a seal key and this install holds the tree secret): a leg that is `no_key` before any network is a `relayUnavailable`, recorded as the failure `no_key`, never a fallback.

connStats.$comment: CONNECTION ANALYTICS (privacy-safe: no content, no user, team, session or device id ever leaves). Every viewer (web, desktop, iOS, Android) and every device serving a feed records eCore event envelopes (packages/ecore `envelope`: {v:1, id, kind, at, source, data}, sessionId OMITTED) and posts them in batches (<= `batchMax`, every `flushMs` and on app background / page hide) to tRPC `connStats.record {events}`; the server validates each against `fields`, drops what fails, stores accepted rows in `steer_connection_events` (no user column) and deletes rows older than `retentionDays`. KINDS: `steer.view` = one per viewer OPEN of a session feed (source `steer-viewer`), recorded twice: phase `settled` once the first frame is applied or `settleAfterMs` passed without one (outcome `ok` | `failed`), and phase `ended` when the viewer closes (with durationMs, fallbacks, reconnects, failures; a view killed with the app has only `settled`). `steer.serve` = one per feed a DEVICE served (source `steer-device`), phase `ended`, path = the carrier it served on. FIELDS: platform (`web` | `desktop` | `ios` | `android` | `cli`), version (the app version string), path (`direct` = an eNet direct iroh path, `iroh_relay` = eNet through an iroh relay, `server_fallback` = the sealed relay tunnel; the carrier that delivered the FIRST frame; absent on a failed settle), firstFrameMs (open -> the first applied frame), errorClass (`errorClasses`; reference `steerViewErrorClass`, cases `errorClassCases` {phase, ok, lastError, background} -> errorClass, #EXP-1678: a FAILED view (settled or ended, no first frame) ALWAYS carries one, never empty and never `other` for want of a failure: `background` when the app or page is in the background at that moment (the OS cut or froze the carriers, which count no failure meanwhile), else the LAST carrier failure, else `dialing` (nothing answered and nothing failed yet: discovery, the eNet join and the relay leg are all still in flight); an OK view carries its last failure, if any, and `background` never), fallbacks (times an AVAILABLE relay leg opened; a `no_key` leg is no fallback, #EXP-1678), reconnects (feed restarts after a first frame), durationMs, failures ({errorClass: count}). DASHBOARD (admin, web-only): per platform and version over a window (24h / 7d / 30d): views (settled), success rate (ok / settled), p50 and p95 firstFrameMs of ok settles, fallback rate (ended views with fallbacks > 0, plus settles whose path is server_fallback, over views). Targets: success >= 99%, p95 first frame < 2000 ms, fallback rare.

a failed settle names the last carrier failure

a failed settle has no path

connStats.$aggregateRule: views = settled rows; successRate = ok settled / views; percentiles = nearest-rank over ok settled firstFrameMs (rank = ceil(p * n), 1-based); fallbackRate = (settled rows with path server_fallback + ended rows with fallbacks > 0 whose path is not server_fallback) / views; every value null when views = 0.

search.$comment: #EDE-96 (phase 3 of #EDE-94, Danny 2026-11-17: search in chat covers the WHOLE chat) SEARCH: a viewer searches what it holds itself (its loaded feed window + the synced messages, at once) and asks the DEVICE that holds the session's journal for the rest. VIEWER → DEVICE `search {requestId, query, beforeSeq?, limit}` (its session is the envelope's, like `history_page`); DEVICE → VIEWER, to the ASKER ONLY, exactly ONE `search_result {requestId, hits: [{seq, kind, snippet, matchStart, matchLen}], total?, done, scannedToSeq}`. Same access rule as every frame (`access`, `viewer_allowed`); same carriers (eNet, or the SEALED RELAY tunnel, where the frames travel inside the same sealed envelope as everything else: nothing about a search reaches the relay in clear). WHO ANSWERS: a live run's publisher (to a JOINED viewer, like `history_page`) and STORED REPLAY (an idle or ENDED row's journal file; a stored search needs no join: an ended row's viewer was dropped at `bye`, its search is answered on its own). Both read the journal FILE (`read_journal_seq`: legacy replay copies dropped), never the in-memory tail; no journal here = `{hits: [], done: true, scannedToSeq: 0}`. WHAT IS SEARCHED = what a viewer would see: `user_message` text (kind `user_message`), `narration` text (`narration`, every lane), a `tool` row's title = `name` + ` ` + `detail` (`tool`), a `tool_update`'s `output` (or, without one, its `diff`) as it is on the wire (already cut to `toolOutputMaxLines`/`toolOutputMaxBytes`, `toolDiffMax*`) with kind `tool_output` and `seq` = the seq of the `tool` row of its id (the row a viewer folds it into; an update whose tool row the journal does not hold is skipped). Never thoughts (their text never leaves the device), slots, questions (synced cards, searched as messages) or anything else. MATCH: a LITERAL substring, case- and diacritics-insensitive: text and query each collapse every run of ASCII whitespace (space, tab, LF, CR, FF, VT) to one space and are trimmed; the query is cut to `queryMaxChars` code points (after the collapse); then both FOLD per code point: NFD, General_Category Mark dropped, lowercased (per code point, no context). A blank query = no hits, done, scannedToSeq 0. ORDER + BOUNDS: the events with seq < `beforeSeq` (absent = all), NEWEST FIRST by seq (a journal read lists its latest-wins slots after the log); one hit per event at most (its FIRST match); `limit` is clamped to [1, `hitsMax`]; `scanned` adds each searched text's UTF-8 bytes (after the collapse). The scan stops after an event once hits reach the limit or scanned reaches `scanMaxBytes`; if events remain below it, `done: false` and the viewer continues with `beforeSeq = scannedToSeq`; else `done: true`. `scannedToSeq` = the seq of the last event examined (0 = none). `total` = hits.length, present only when the whole journal was searched in this answer (no `beforeSeq` and done). SNIPPET (offsets in CODE POINTS of the snippet): over the collapsed text, from = max(0, matchStart - `snippetLeadChars`), to = min(len, max(from + `snippetChars`, matchEnd)); `…` prefixed when from > 0 and appended when to < len; matchStart = its offset inside the snippet (after any `…`), matchLen = the match's length in the collapsed text. Reference `steerSearch({events, query, beforeSeq, limit, scanMaxBytes})` (the `cases`; `scanMaxBytes` absent = the constant). A viewer keeps ONE search in flight and drops a `search_result` for any other requestId; a hit `kind` it does not know is skipped.
